pr_title: Fix code splitting with interop shared bundle
pr_body:
# ↪️ Pull Request

When a shared module, that is defined as a common js module, is used in a parent and child bundle, it is not resolved the same way in both bundles.
The `__esModule` is removed/ not set at all, therefore the interop check is wrong and reference errors are the result.

Fixes #3686.

When a `require` call is used, the asset is marked as `isCommonJS`: [hoist.js#L339](https://github.com/parcel-bundler/parcel/blob/v2/packages/shared/scope-hoisting/src/hoist.js#L339)
As far as I understand, due to scope hoisting, the `require` call is removed and therefore the import is detected as an unused value: [link.js#L341](https://github.com/parcel-bundler/parcel/blob/v2/packages/shared/scope-hoisting/src/link.js#L341)
Therefore the `__esModule` flag is not injected: [link.js#L361](https://github.com/parcel-bundler/parcel/blob/v2/packages/shared/scope-hoisting/src/link.js#L361)

Inserting the `__esModule` flag always, in case the `require `call was removed and the `isCommonJS` flag is not set, solves the issue for me.

## 💻 Examples

See https://github.com/parcel-bundler/parcel/issues/3686, https://github.com/parcel-bundler/parcel/issues/3686#issuecomment-549055131 or the tests added in the pr.

## ✔️ PR Todo

- [x] Added/updated unit tests for this change
- [x] Fix second integration test

issue_context.title: v2: code splitting with `process` in shared module throws in child bundle
comments:
The main bundle uses (and therefore contains) `styled-components`. The async child bundle also uses that package, and imports it via `$parcel$interopDefault(parcelRequire(....))`. 
The issue here is that the main bundle seems to have optimized away the `$...styled-components....$exports.__esModule = true;` statement (therefore `$parcel$interopDefaul` fails in the child bundle and it won't find the `default` export, it treats `styled-components` as a CJS module).

Thank you so much for reporting all these bugs!

I found out, because of `process`, `require('process')` is injected by parcel. Therefore, styled-components are marked as a common js module which then causes issues.
I added test cases and some more details here: https://github.com/parcel-bundler/parcel/pull/3730

Maybe someone has better ideas on how to resolve this, my current attempt does not look proper so far.

@mischnic I tried the nightly release in my project. Unfortunately, since we added the check for `bundleGraph.isAssetReferencedByAnotherBundleOfType(mod, 'js')`, the fix does not work in the project longer.

I am using multiple nested imports (so at least one time a dynamic import requests another dynamic import), maybe this is related.

Also, I use Typescript with JSX inside the project. But I assume `bundleGraph.isAssetReferencedByAnotherBundleOfType(mod, 'js')` should also work for typescript files, correct?

If I replace `isReferenced` with `let isReferenced = true`, it works as expected.

Any thoughts or ideas? If not I would need to put some more effort into creating a reproducible example/ tests.

Should we reopen this ticket?

😞 

> `bundleGraph.isAssetReferencedByAnotherBundleOfType(mod, 'js')` should also work for typescript files, correct?

A typescript asset is transpiled into a javascript asset which becomes a javascript bundle, so yes.

I created a minimal example here: https://github.com/garthenweb/parcel-bug-report-examples/tree/bug/missing-esmodules-in-child-bundle

This is now an example without styled-components, as I found that it also fails using react standalone.

In a bigger project, it was randomly throwing for react but also for styled-components.

Actually, I figured that `let isReferenced = true` did not help in this case.
So I am not sure if this is still the same issue, but at least related as the `__esModule` flag is missing when requested in a child bundle via `parcelRequire("12345");`, so it looks highly related.

> From what I understand some information in asset.meta is out of sync when running parcel with multiple workers. But this is more guessing.

🕵👍 
PR to fix that (with an explanation): https://github.com/parcel-bundler/parcel/pull/4370
Nice! I can confirm it fixes this issue and would also close this ticket again.
Checked it one more time with `2.0.0-nightly.171` and it is still working! Therefore the ticket can be closed.

review_comments: Was there a reason why `isCommonJS` was checked here? From my point of view, it does not matter as long as it is an es6 module with a default export.
